model_annotations.English: The chart illustrates per-block “Sensitivity” values across a sequence of model blocks, with bar color indicating whether a block is assigned 4‑Fbit (blue) or 2‑Fbit (green) precision. The horizontal axis contains the categories as integer “Block Index” values running from 0 to 63 (shown with labeled ticks at 0, 15, 31, 47, and 63) on a linear scale. The vertical axis is labeled “Sensitivity” and is displayed on a logarithmic scale, with major tick labels at approximately \(10^{-5}\) and \(10^{-4}\) (shown as dashed horizontal grid lines); the plotted values span from a few \(\times 10^{-6}\) at the low end up to a few \(\times 10^{-4}\) at the high end. Each block index is represented by a single vertical bar (not stacked), with most early indices (near 0–28) shown as green 2‑Fbit bars at roughly \(\sim 2\times 10^{-6}\) to \(\sim 2\times 10^{-5}\), including a very short bar in the low \(10^{-6}\) range and several around \(10^{-5}\). Around the low 30s there is a small cluster of blue 4‑Fbit bars (roughly in the \(\sim 3\times 10^{-5}\) to \(\sim 4\times 10^{-5}\) range) interleaved with adjacent green bars of similar magnitude, followed by additional mixed green and occasional blue bars through the mid‑40s that generally sit between about \(2\times 10^{-5}\) and \(6\times 10^{-5}\). From the high‑40s into the 60s, many bars are blue 4‑Fbit and rise into and above the \(10^{-4}\) decade, with the tallest bars near the final indices (around 60–63) reaching on the order of \(\sim 2\times 10^{-4}\) to \(\sim 3\times 10^{-4}\); there is also an isolated green bar in the early‑50s among otherwise blue neighbors. The bars are arranged in increasing block-index order (not sorted by value), and there are no additional visual emphases such as outlines, callouts, or numeric annotations beyond the legend identifying the two color encodings.
model_annotations.German: The chart illustrates per-block “Sensitivity” values across a sequence of model blocks, with bars colored by precision setting (blue for “4-Fbit” and green for “2-Fbit”) as indicated by the legend in the upper-left. The horizontal axis contains the categories as block positions labeled “Block Index,” shown in increasing order from 0 to 63 with tick labels at 0, 15, 31, 47, and 63. The vertical axis is the value axis labeled “Sensitivity” and is displayed on a logarithmic scale, with major tick labels at approximately \(10^{-5}\) and \(10^{-4}\) (and corresponding dashed horizontal gridlines), spanning values from a few \(\times 10^{-6}\) up to a few \(\times 10^{-4}\). Each bar represents the sensitivity for a given block index; most blocks are shown as green (2-Fbit) bars through the earlier and mid indices, with intermittent blue (4-Fbit) bars appearing around the low 30s and mid 40s, and then many consecutive blue bars in the later indices (roughly the high 40s through 63), plus one isolated green bar within that late region. Visually, the smallest bars occur in the early indices (around block indices near 4–7), reaching down to roughly \(2\text{–}4\times 10^{-6}\), while many mid-range bars sit around the \(10^{-5}\) to several \(\times 10^{-5}\) range; the tallest bars appear near the end (around indices 60–63), extending above the \(10^{-4}\) line to roughly \(2\text{–}3\times 10^{-4}\). The bars are not sorted by height; they follow the block index order, and there are no additional annotations or special visual emphasis beyond the two-color encoding and the legend.
